accuracy.evidence: Checked CCSS 1.OA.6 add/subtract within 20 with make-ten and decompose-leading-to-a-ten examples (8+6, 13−4 style) against NC Y1/Y2 related facts.

misconceptions.evidence: Checked traps: stick-digits (8+6 as 86); stopping at 10 without adding the leftover; recounting from 1 instead of counting on.

lab_distinct.evidence: Checked flagw20: make-ten past 10 + decompose-to-ten take-away; not flagsum10 (fluent within 10), flagnb20 (exact bonds ≤20), or flagnbonds (exact make-10 partners).

lab_teaches.evidence: Checked: learner fills toward 10, bridges 8+6 via make-ten, breaks 13−5 to a ten, uses related 16−7, picks count-on, spots stick-digits myth.

predictions.evidence: Checked tempting wrongs on empty-to-ten, make-ten total, break-to-ten result, related part, count-on vs recount, and stick-digits myth.

challenge_feedback.evidence: Checked why() splits stick-digits, stop-at-10, echo number, add/sub sign mix, recount-from-1, and related-fact jumbles.

readability.evidence: Checked ages 6–7 kid lines use make ten / count on / related; adult names CCSS 1.OA.6 and common slips within family bars.

no_filler.evidence: Checked every sentence teaches a within-20 strategy, ten-frame bridge, related fact, or named mix-up.

mobile.evidence: Checked dual ten-frame chip rows and break-to-ten slider with large lbtn twins; layout holds near 390 px width.

accessibility.evidence: Checked split/bridge/break buttons twin every canvas gesture; live aria-label on the figure; challenge uses aria-live status.

sources: CCSS 1.OA.6 Add and subtract within 20; make ten; decompose leading to a ten
